# the contributor audit of complete parity cores and fine-hyperplane recovery

Read both full literal proofs:

* `candidate ff31d56304dd901a`;
* `candidate 6f79052f99c749c4`.


qualification in the recovery note clarified by its author during
audit. Neither is a proof of unrestricted OC.

## Complete parity core

The ordinary compactness input is uniform in the class of individual
bodies. Sending any maximum inscribed simplex to the standard simplex
puts the normalized body in a fixed box; a limiting depth-Gamma body
must itself be a simplex. Its maximum inscribed-simplex volume remains
that of the fixed standard simplex, forcing the limit to equal it.
Thus the conclusion holds uniformly over all choices of bodies and
normalizations, not just one fixed sequence.

For each partner, opposite translations put zero in the small endpoint
and the other endpoint inside twice the middle body. Both endpoints
are then bounded uniformly. These are identities for paired cap
thresholds, not separate changes to the actual source. Uniform
ordinary rigidity and the near-equal volume ratio make the partner's
maximum inscribed-simplex volume tend to the middle volume. This
justifies the determinant threshold uniformly over arbitrarily many
pairs. The centered-row Hadamard inequality gives at least J good
facets for each endpoint point, with a fixed positive margin. Their
indices may vary pointwise; integrating their actual indicator sets
gives the required average credit without assigning one fixed facet.

The endpoint-copy argument supplies those SAME fixed credits under
the later small normal and center perturbations, for every real tilt.
All widths and perturbation errors are uniform in the translated
pair frame. The repaired center is the TRUE middle centroid plus
the balanced displacement from the aggregate credits. Its size is
O(e/V) where e is that star's actual mass, and it lies in the actual
middle body. Proper-section continuity gives a fixed small density
error, which is integrated only over this O(e/V) displacement.
Consequently the total error is eta e, even if this star's mass is
arbitrarily smaller than the source's total outside mass. The exact
ordinary Grunbaum baseline incurs no Hausdorff-volume error of its
own. The remaining normals have a fixed simplex gap; the zero
continuous normal includes the entire middle fiber. These checks
prove the local statement for arbitrary finite star size with
constants depending only on d.

The global parity step needs no empty-polytope property. An outside
base has a unique core parity partner. Their integer midpoint would
carry at least 2^-d times the minimum core volume, even if the original
outside fiber is null. Small total outside mass therefore forces that
midpoint into the core. Within one target star the partners are all
distinct, so no source fiber is counted twice. A single ambient tilt
gives one of the arbitrary lists of paired thresholds already covered
by the lemma.

Failure of the requested bound implies every ordinary core maximal
depth times its volume is below the common target. Summing the
resulting upper volume bounds around a minimum-volume core proves
max V-min V<E, uniformly in 2^n. The same inequality forces every
ordinary depth to be at most Gamma(1+E/min V). Thus ALL local lemma
hypotheses follow from one dimension-only smallness threshold. An
empty star uses its ordinary centroid. Averaging the repaired scores
gives a strict excess because the credit coefficient alpha exceeds
Gamma. A single actual core center is then selected from a finite
list. Boundary-through-point reductions, oblique directions, and
whole-fiber boundary mass are all explicit. Positive core fibers
ensure q=d and positive finite fiber-sum measure.

## Fine-hyperplane nonconcentration

The lattice transference proof is correct. Greedy shortest independent
vectors realize the successive minima. Diagonal scaling in their
orthogonal flag puts every nonzero lattice vector outside the open
unit ball: take its last nonzero flag coordinate and compare with
the corresponding greedy minimum. Half-ball packing proves the
needed determinant/product bound. The cofactor functional takes
integer values on the original lattice, so supplies the short dual
vector; rounding in the generated sublattice bounds the original
covering radius. This proves the stated explicit constant without
invoking a sharp transference theorem.

Dual-level counting uses actual hyperplane masses and includes
boundary atoms. It is invariant under the block normalizations
because their fine-section Jacobian is constant. In each coarse
fiber of positive limiting FINE mass, vanishing conditional
hyperplane concentration forces full sampled base rank and hence
a full coarse body. A volume-one block normalization then makes
its lattice covering radius vanish, and the exact block determinant
identity proves fine mass divided by ordinary coarse volume tends
to one.

For an integer convex combination target, a translated homothetic
copy of any retained source body lies in its actual target fiber.
Apply the one-source block map to that COPY and translate its center
back into a fixed ball. The lattice coset offset may vary arbitrarily,
but the covering radius and the uniform sampling estimate do not.
This gives a positive limiting target fine mass and proves closure
of the retained base set. It also yields total retained ordinary
volume asymptotic to the entire original fine mass, so the omitted
fine mass condition is derived rather than assumed.

Rescaling one anchor map per dependence component to determinant
1/M_ret preserves density. Incidence comparison and the previous
full-shape lift theorem now apply, and actual centers are recovered
by rounding in their actual cosets before mapping back. The bound
for an individual lift limit is explicitly along the subsequence
producing that limit; the universal full-sequence bound is obtained
by first taking a subsequence realizing its liminf. This was the
only wording clarification requested during audit.

The three equal sampled slices have maximum hyperplane fraction
1/3 but permanently non-dense mesh in every uniformly round block
frame. This correctly refutes density from a mere sub-half bound,
without making an adverse claim about their actual halfspace depth.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
